title: All we know about Zika so far...
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant give an overview of the 2015-2016 Zika virus outbreak: its 1947 discovery in a Rhesus monkey in Uganda, its spread across dozens of countries, symptoms, the link to microcephaly and Guillain-Barré syndrome, transmission by Aedes aegypti mosquitoes and sexual contact, mosquito control proposals (transgenic mosquitoes, Wolbachia), vaccine development, US funding fights, local transmission in Miami and Puerto Rico, diagnosis, and a listener mail segment about the British "bacon buddy." Hosts stress the information was current only as of recording and is not medical advice.

National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases

segments.title: Opening and framing the Zika outbreak
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the episode as a breaking-news overview, note that information dates quickly, and discuss public apathy versus fear and the history of Zika's discovery in 1947 in Uganda and early human cases.

segments.title: Symptoms, Guillain-Barré, and the microcephaly link
segments.summary: Hosts list Zika symptoms, note that most infections are asymptomatic, discuss the suspected link to Guillain-Barré syndrome, and explain why the WHO issued an emergency alert over microcephaly cases in Brazil.

segments.title: How microcephaly affects babies
segments.summary: Hosts describe how Zika is thought to attack developing brain stem cells, the resulting brain damage in babies, reported NPR findings, and the estimated increase in microcephaly rates among infected pregnant women.

segments.title: Mosquitoes and mosquito control
segments.summary: Hosts identify the Aedes aegypti yellow fever mosquito as the vector and discuss eradication ideas, transgenic mosquitoes tested by Oxitec in Brazil, and the Wolbachia bacteria approach, along with ecological concerns.

segments.title: How Zika spreads: mosquito bites and sexual transmission
segments.summary: Hosts explain how mosquitoes pick up the virus and transmit it through saliva, and discuss sexual transmission, including semen, saliva, and vaginal secretions, and Brian Foy's earlier unfunded research warning.

segments.title: Zika vaccine development
segments.summary: Hosts discuss vaccine efforts, including a company in India and an NIAID DNA plasmid vaccine approach that had been tested in phase one and is similar to a West Nile approach, and the risk of public funding drying up.

segments.title: US funding fight, Miami, and Puerto Rico
segments.summary: Hosts cover the Congressional refusal of Obama's emergency Zika funding request, CDC reallocation of Ebola and emergency funds, the CDC travel advisory for a Miami neighborhood, and the spread in Puerto Rico and its effect on tourism, plus theme park mosquito spray.

segments.title: Diagnosis, precautions, and the Olympics
segments.summary: Hosts describe how Zika is diagnosed through travel history, blood and urine tests, and warn against taking NSAIDs like Advil before diagnosis because of dengue hemorrhage risk. They also note the Olympics had no reported Zika cases and mention the geographic range of the mosquito.

segments.title: Listener mail: bacon buddy
segments.summary: A listener from Kent, England writes about the British 'buddy' sandwich, including the bacon buddy and chip buddy, and the cheesy dunkers snack.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts give social media and website contact information and close the episode.
